nodes.description: As in type 2A, active intestinal calcium absorption fails in the presence of abundant calcitriol, producing hypocalcemia, secondary hyperparathyroidism and phosphaturia. This is the disorder-specific instance of the module's calciopenic trigger arm; the substitution relative to type 2A is that the block is at response-element occupancy rather than at the receptor protein.

evidence.snippet: Clinically apparent hereditary vitamin D-resistant rickets (HVDRR) usually results from a loss of function mutation in the vitamin D receptor (VDR). We recently described a human with the classical HVDRR phenotype but normal VDR function.

nodes.description: Overexpressed heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein C1/C2 acts as a response-element-binding protein, occupying vitamin D response elements in target gene promoters. The vitamin D receptor-retinoid X receptor dimer binds hormone normally and is recruited normally, but the normal cyclical exchange of receptor on and off the response element is displaced by the competing protein, so transactivation fails. The mechanism is a transcriptional interference effect rather than a defect in any component of the vitamin D pathway itself.

evidence.snippet: Hormone resistance resulted from constitutive overexpression of heterogeneous nuclear ribonucleoprotein (hnRNP) that competed with a normally functioning VDR-retinoid X receptor (RXR) dimer for binding to the vitamin D response element (VDRE).

evidence.snippet: When overexpressed in vitamin D-responsive cells, cDNAs for both hnRNPC1 and hnRNPC2 inhibited VDR-VDRE-directed transactivation (28 and 43%, respectively; both p < 0.005).
